Why stacked headers matter

Three overlapping fixed bars reduce the visible reading area to a narrow strip, so any floating control has to avoid them as well as the selection itself.

Designers add banners one at a time, and nobody measures the combined height until a reader complains about the cramped space left over for the actual story.

A good extension treats the viewport as the only reliable coordinate space and never assumes that the top of the window is free.

Filler paragraph so the page can scroll: the harbour was quiet, the tide was out, and the gulls stood in neat rows along the breakwater waiting for something to happen.

Another filler paragraph with a few more words to extend the page, since scrolling behaviour is exactly where placement code tends to fail.

The last paragraph closes the article with a gentle reminder that headers should serve readers, not the other way around.
